question: On 24 March 2026, the Israeli Knesset’s National Security Committee approved, for final readings, a discriminatory death penalty bill designed to apply exclusively to Palestinians, including through military legal structures in the occupied Palestinian territory. Executions would reportedly be carried out by hanging within 90 days of sentencing, with no possibility of pardon or commutation.

The final vote on the proposal is imminent. UN experts have warned1 that the bill would violate the most fundamental principles of international human rights law, including the right to life, fair-trial guarantees, and the prohibition of torture and ill-treatment. It would also constitute a grave violation of international humanitarian law. Can the Council clarify: 1.
what concrete measures it will propose or support in response to these developments?
whether it will ensure that the current package of EU measures is updated, including with the addition of possible restrictive measures against those responsible?
answer: The European Union takes a principled stance against the death penalty in all cases and in all circumstances.

In the Statement of 31 March 20261 by the High Representative on behalf of the European Union, the EU noted that the Israeli Parliament’s approval of the Death Penalty Bill marked a serious regression from Israel’s long-held practice of a de facto moratorium on both executions and capital punishment sentencing, and expressed its deep concern over the de facto discriminatory character of the bill.

In keeping with the EU’s global efforts towards universal abolition of the death penalty, the EU urged Israel to abide by its previous, principled position and by its obligations under international law, as well to honour its commitment to democratic principles, which are also reflected in the provisions of the EU-Israel Association Agreement.

As regards the Commission proposals related to the EU-Israel Association Agreement, the Council recalls its reply to Written Question E-002313/2025, and that the Foreign Affairs Council has addressed the matter in the context of its discussions on the situation in the Middle East.
